slides.title: PART 01 • CONCEPTS
slides.html:
PART 01 • CONCEPTS

What is Deployment?

Transitioning code from your local computer to the global internet

CORE CONCEPT

Local Development (localhost:3000)

Runs solely on your machine inside Node.js. Only accessible by you via local loopback. Stops when your computer closes or terminal shuts down.

$ pnpm run dev
Ready in 1200ms on http://localhost:3000

Production Deployment (Public Internet)

Packaged, optimized, and hosted on high-availability cloud servers around the world. Accessible 24/7/365 by millions of users with automated HTTPS.

Production URL: https://taskflow.com
Response time: 24ms from Global Edge Network

slides.title: PART 01 • EXECUTION MODELS
slides.html:
PART 01 • EXECUTION MODELS

Static Websites vs Fullstack Applications

Understanding execution models: Static Files, SSR, and Serverless APIs

Static Sites (SSG / HTML)

Pure HTML, CSS, and JS generated ahead of time during build. Served directly from Edge CDN storage with zero server computation.

Server-Rendered (SSR)

HTML is rendered on-demand for every visitor request via Serverless Functions. Ideal for dynamic dashboards and personalized feeds.

Serverless APIs & Actions

Isolated backend compute executing on demand without maintaining continuous servers. Scales from 0 to thousands of concurrent requests.

slides.title: PART 02 • PLATFORM OVERVIEW
slides.html:
PART 02 • PLATFORM OVERVIEW

What is Vercel?

The native cloud platform for Next.js and the modern web

VERCEL

Engineered by the Creators of Next.js

Vercel created and maintains Next.js. The platform is purpose-built to extract maximum performance from the App Router, Server Components, and Server Actions.

Zero Server Management

No configuring Nginx, Ubuntu servers, Docker files, or PM2 process managers. Push your code to Git, and Vercel handles all infrastructure automatically.

slides.title: PART 02 • CORE FEATURES
slides.html:
PART 02 • CORE FEATURES

Core Platform Capabilities

Git automation, Global Edge Network, Serverless functions, and instant previews

1. Continuous Git Deployment

Automatic builds on every git push. Pull requests generate live staging preview URLs instantly for team review.

2. Global Edge Network (CDN)

Static assets and cached responses distributed to 300+ Point of Presence (PoP) locations across the globe for sub-50ms latency.

3. Serverless Compute

Backend Route Handlers and Server Actions spin up instantly in response to requests, scaling to zero when inactive.

4. Automated Security & SSL

Free automated Let's Encrypt TLS certificates, DDoS mitigation, and enterprise-grade DNS infrastructure.

slides.title: PART 10 • SECURITY BOUNDARY
slides.html:
PART 10 • SECURITY BOUNDARY

The NEXT_PUBLIC_* Security Boundary

Preventing client bundle leakage of private server secrets

CRITICAL

Server-Only (Secret)

DATABASE_URL, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY

Never prefixed with NEXT_PUBLIC_. Only accessible inside Server Components, Route Handlers, and Server Actions.

Client-Exposed (Public)

NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME, NEXT_PUBLIC_MAP_KEY

Inlined directly into browser JavaScript bundle during build. Accessible by anyone viewing website source.

The Redeployment Requirement

Why updated environment variables require a new deployment

IMPORTANT
Updating an environment variable does NOT automatically update existing deployments! Next.js inlines variables during compilation. You must trigger a Redeploy in the dashboard or push a new commit to apply updated variables.

Client Components ('use client')

Handles browser interactivity, state, event listeners, and hooks (useState, useEffect). Hydrated on the user's browser.

slides.title: PART 13 • EMAIL SAFETY
slides.html:
PART 13 • EMAIL SAFETY

Preserving Email DNS Records

Avoiding email disruption by protecting MX, SPF, DKIM, and DMARC

DANGER ZONE
NEVER DELETE MX RECORDS! If you have Google Workspace or Outlook email connected to your domain, only add the required A or CNAME record. Do not switch nameservers or wipe existing MX, TXT (SPF), or DKIM records, or company email will break instantly.

slides.title: PART 13 • PROPAGATION
slides.html:
PART 13 • PROPAGATION

DNS Propagation & Automatic SSL

Let's Encrypt TLS certificate generation and HTTPS enforcement

Zero-Config Automatic SSL

Once DNS records point to Vercel, Vercel automatically requests and provisions a Let's Encrypt TLS certificate. Certificates are renewed automatically before expiration with zero manual intervention.

slides.title: PART 14 • SECURITY
slides.html:
PART 14 • SECURITY

HTTPS & Transport Security

HSTS headers, modern TLS cipher suites, and redirect rules

HTTP -> HTTPS Redirect

All insecure port 80 HTTP requests are automatically redirected with 308 Permanent Redirect to secure port 443 HTTPS.

HSTS Header

HTTP Strict Transport Security forces modern browsers to communicate only over encrypted channels.

slides.title: PART 14 • HARDENING
slides.html:
PART 14 • HARDENING

Application Hardening on Vercel

Content Security Policy (CSP), rate limiting, and input sanitization

Security Headers in next.config.js

Configure X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, and Content Security Policy (CSP) headers to prevent XSS and clickjacking attacks.

slides.title: PART 14 • AUDITING
slides.html:
PART 14 • AUDITING

Secret Auditing & Remediation

Scanning repositories for leaks and rotating compromised credentials

If You Accidentally Push a Secret:

1. Immediately rotate / invalidate the key in your Neon or Stripe dashboard.
2. Deleting the commit in Git is NOT enough because commit history preserves the secret.
3. Generate a brand new credential and update Vercel environment variables.

PART 15 • THE MIGRATION TRAP

The Code vs Database Rollback Discrepancy

Why rolling back code does NOT undo database schema changes

CRITICAL WARNING
Vercel rollback ONLY reverts web frontend and serverless code! It cannot un-drop database tables or rollback destructive SQL migrations on Neon. Design migrations to be backward-compatible with the previous release.

Differentiating compile-time failures from production exceptions

Captures pnpm install and next build. Look here when deployment status shows red failed build. Common causes: TypeScript, ESLint, missing packages.

Runtime Logs (Production)

Streams live execution logs of Serverless Functions and Route Handlers. Look here when users see 500 Server Errors or database timeout exceptions.

Missing dependencies, TypeScript errors, and incorrect root directory

Error: Module not found: Can't resolve 'clsx'
Cause: Package installed globally or missing from package.json dependencies.
Solution: Run pnpm add clsx locally, commit package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml, then push.

Hobby plan serverless functions have a 10s execution limit (expandable to 60s on Pro). Avoid long loops, un-indexed slow queries, or hanging external API calls.

slides.title: PART 21 • MISTAKES
slides.html:
PART 21 • MISTAKES

Top 10 Costly Deployment Mistakes

Critical errors developers make and exact steps to avoid them

AVOID THESE

1. Forgetting to Redeploy after updating Env Vars

Changing an env var doesn't update old builds. Must trigger Redeploy.

2. Committing .env.local to GitHub

Scrapers will steal keys within seconds. Keep it strictly in .gitignore.

3. Deleting MX records when configuring DNS

Wiping existing MX records will kill your company's Google/Outlook email.

4. Exposing secret keys with NEXT_PUBLIC_

Never put database passwords or secret keys behind NEXT_PUBLIC_.
